newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS -DOWN ON CRUDE, JET FUEL SLIDES.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS -DOWN ON CRUDE, JET FUEL SLIDES.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were weaker at midday on Friday on lower overnight crude values with jet fuel coming under further pressure after physical sellers emerged at lower levels late on Thursday, traders said.
Gas oil, jet fuel and naphtha lost more than 20 cents per barrel as poor regional fundamentals came back to haunt the market after its recent rally on the back of the stronger crude.
The August jet fuel/gas oil spread narrowed sharply after several physical sellers offered cargoes at around $23.50 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
The offered price was only 50 cents per barrel above the gas oil selling price.
As a result, the August regrade was last quoted at 65/80 cents from Thursday's $1.00/$1.20, brokers said. August regrade traded mid-week at $1.20.
The forward fourth quarter and first quarter regrades are holding steady at above $2.00 due to expected strong demand in winter.
Gas oil prices dipped in line with the 30-cent drop to overnight September Brent crude which closed at $18.90 on the International Petroleum Exchange.
August gas oil was last quoted at $22.75/$22.85 per barrel, down from Wednesday's $22.95/$23.05. August traded earlier in the day at $22.80 and $22.83, brokers said.
September was also quoted down at $23.25/$23.33, from Wednesday's $23.45/$23.55, brokers said. It traded in the morning at $23.30 and $23.25, they said.
The August/September time spread remains unchanged at minus 45 cents to minus 55 cents and traded earlier at minus 50 cents, brokers said.

In the physical market on Thursday, a 240,000-barrel cargoes were offered at between $23.00 to $23.20 per barrel for loading over the next 15-30 days, allowing for a 10-cent contango for each five-day window, traders said.
August naphtha was last quoted at $21.35/$21.55 per barrel, down from Thursday's $21.70/$21.90, brokers said.
Fuel oil relatively more steady as prices edged down about 25 cents as the market looked to improved bunker demand for support.
August and September were last quoted at $102.00/$103.00, down from Thursday's $102.50/$103.00, brokers said.
